clue.text: Doctor vents one lung — making news programme's introduction showing individuals that require a helping hand?

definitions.text: individuals that require a helping hand?

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters are rearranged

parts.words: vents one lung — making news programme's introduction
parts.note: take the words vents one lung, which hold three Ns (read news as N's), and make each N into P, the introduction to programme

explanation.surface: A medic drains a patient's lung while a news bulletin opens on puppets.
explanation.walkthrough: VENTS ONE LUNG holds three Ns; 'making news programme's introduction' turns every N into P, the first letter of 'programme', giving VEPTSOPELUPG, which 'Doctor' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Glove puppets are worked by a hand inside them, so each one literally needs a hand to move.

clue.text: On the contrary, some lemon grass gives a little garden whimsy?

indicators.note: on the contrary means the opposite way round, so the letters run backwards
some means only a portion of the words that follow is used

parts.note: the letters are taken from inside these words

explanation.surface: Planting some lemon grass adds a small whimsical touch to a garden.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across the gap between the two words, read right to left.
explanation.definitionFit: A gnome is a small ornamental figure placed in gardens for fun, a whimsical decoration.

clue.text: They make cubes — but nothing's squared?

parts.note: O, the round zero figure, means nothing
squared means multiplied by itself: a times sign (X) and the same zero figure again

explanation.surface: A maths puzzle: cubes are made, but zero squared stays as nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: Squaring a number is multiplying it by itself, written with a times sign, so nothing squared is zero, times, zero.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxo is a British brand of stock cubes, so the company makes cubes for gravy and soup.

clue.text: Quorate assembly reaches halfway point?

indicators.note: assembly means putting parts together, so the letters are built into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A meeting with enough members present reaches the middle of its agenda.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'point' is not a stage of a meeting but a pole of the Earth.
explanation.definitionFit: The equator is the line around the Earth equidistant from both poles, midway between those two points.

clue.text: See 1
Discourage injured Rooney dropping back at World Cup

indicators.note: injured means hurt or damaged, so the letters are put out of order
dropping back means the name loses its final letter

parts.note: taken as written; Wayne Rooney is an England footballer
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An injured Wayne Rooney, the England striker, has to drop out of his position at the World Cup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dropping back' sounds like a footballer's positional move, but it removes the Y at the end of ROONEY before the whole fodder is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To pour cold water on an idea is an idiom for dampening enthusiasm, which is to discourage it.

clue.text: There will be correspondence in this paper principally over street fight

definitions.text: There will be correspondence in this

indicators.note: principally means at the start, so only the leading letter is used

parts.note: first letter taken
O is the cricket abbreviation for over
ST is the address abbreviation for street
to box is to fight with fists

explanation.surface: A newspaper reports a street brawl and expects readers' letters.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters page of a paper is suggested, but the definition is where letters are posted.
explanation.definitionFit: A postbox is where letters are posted for collection, so mail is found inside it.

clue.text: Arranged lower fee if taking time to deliver more than 7,000 tonnes of iron

indicators.note: taking means holding within, so the time letter sits inside
arranged means set in order, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written
T is the physics abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A haulier agrees a lower fee if given extra time to deliver a huge load of iron.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of LOWER FEE IF is built around T; the definition is a fact about the structure rather than a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: The Eiffel Tower in Paris is a wrought-iron structure whose metal weighs roughly 7,300 tonnes.

clue.text: Wide-ranging knowledge supported by computer's data retrieval

indicators.note: supported by means in this down clue the first piece sits above the next

parts.note: SP, from starting price, is slang for the inside information on something
a readout is data retrieved and displayed by a computer

explanation.surface: Broad knowledge backed up by data a computer has fetched.
explanation.walkthrough: SP is British racing slang: the starting price, and so the inside information on anything ('what's the SP?').
explanation.definitionFit: Something spread out covers a large area, so it is extensive or wide-ranging.

clue.text: American city hotel putting Yoko and, reportedly, John Lennon up initially

parts.note: H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
Yoko Ono, the artist married to John Lennon

indicators.note: reportedly means the word is taken by its sound, as if heard rather than read

parts.note: john is slang for a toilet, a loo

indicators.note: initially means take only the opening letter of each of the two words that follow

parts.note: first letter taken
first letter taken

explanation.surface: A hotel booking puts Yoko and John Lennon up in a room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'John' looks like Lennon's first name but is slang for a loo, and LOO said aloud is spelt LU; then L and U are the first letters of 'Lennon up'.
explanation.definitionFit: Honolulu is the capital of Hawaii, a state of the USA, so it is a city in America.

clue.text: Peter Parker ultimately being more cautious

parts.note: peter is old criminal slang for a safe, hence peterman for a safecracker

indicators.note: ultimately means take only the final letter of the following word

parts.note: last letter taken

explanation.surface: Spider-Man's alter ego Peter Parker finally learns to take fewer risks.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter Parker reads as Spider-Man's name, but 'Peter' is thieves' slang for a safe and 'ultimately' takes the R ending 'Parker'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being safer means taking fewer risks, which is the same as being more careful or cautious.

clue.text: Tyrant's 'psychic powers' inspired by E — according to coded dispatch

indicators.note: inspired by means breathed into, so the psychic letters go inside the other word

parts.note: in Morse code, used for coded telegraph messages, the letter E is a single dot
ESP, extrasensory perception

explanation.surface: A tyrant's supposed mind-reading is fed by coded messages.
explanation.walkthrough: Morse code, used for telegraph dispatches, renders the letter E as one short signal. The 's after Tyrant stands for 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A despot is a ruler holding absolute power, often cruelly, which is what a tyrant is.

clue.text: Writing a year off after regularly consulting ballot box

indicators.note: after means the rearranged letters follow the alternate ones

parts.note: to pen is to write, used here for writing

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter is taken

parts.note: alternate letters taken

indicators.note: off means gone bad or wrong, so these letters are disordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone stops writing for a year after counting votes from a ballot box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ballot box' looks like one phrase, but 'box' is the definition: in football the penalty area is called the box.
explanation.definitionFit: In football the marked zone in front of each goal, where fouls give penalties, is commonly called the box.

clue.text: 100 not entirely competent people backing one that can climb to the top?

definitions.text: one that can climb to the top?

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100

indicators.note: not entirely means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: able means competent

indicators.note: backing means the word for people is read in reverse order

parts.note: a race is a people or nation

explanation.surface: A hundred people backing someone not wholly capable of reaching the summit.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition sounds like a climber or ambitious person, but it is a vehicle hauled up a mountainside on a wire.
explanation.definitionFit: A cable car is hauled up mountainsides on a wire, so it is a vehicle built to ascend to the summit.

clue.text: Garden in East End requires work

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for East

indicators.note: something that requires work is not yet in order, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A garden in London's East End needs some tending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'East End' reads as the area of London, but splits into E for East and END to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Eden is the paradise garden where the Bible places Adam and Eve.

clue.text: Provide disc to correct software problem without lead for laptop — if it crashes it could be disastrous

definitions.text: if it crashes it could be disastrous

parts.note: to do can mean to provide, as in they do lunches
O is a round shape, a disc

indicators.note: without means outside, so the debug letters wrap around the other letter

parts.note: to debug is to fix faults in software

indicators.note: lead for means the opening letter of the word that follows

parts.note: first letter taken

explanation.surface: A technician supplies a disc to fix a laptop bug, warning that a crash would be disastrous.
explanation.walkthrough: The computer crash of the surface becomes a bomb hitting the ground: a doodlebug was the Second World War V-1 flying bomb.
explanation.definitionFit: The V-1 flying bomb, nicknamed the doodlebug, exploded on impact, so its crashing caused destruction.

clue.text: Recreation in New Orleans with taxi seconds away

indicators.note: new signals that the letters are made into something new, a rearrangement
away means the seconds letter is removed from the city's name

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Leisure time in New Orleans, riding around in a cab.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New Orleans' looks like the city; 'New' is the anagram signal, and 'seconds away' drops the S from ORLEANS before ORLEANTAXI is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Relaxation is rest and leisure taken for enjoyment, which is what recreation means.

clue.text: Microsoft product, Excel finally breaks — another is pointless for China, say

indicators.note: breaks means the letter splits the program name, sitting inside it

parts.note: Word is Microsoft's word processor

indicators.note: finally means only the closing letter of the spreadsheet's name is taken

parts.note: last letter taken

indicators.note: pointless means the program name loses the word point

parts.note: another Microsoft product: PowerPoint, the slideshow program

explanation.surface: An office worker complains that Word, Excel and PowerPoint all keep crashing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Excel finally' gives L, which 'breaks' WORD. 'Another' is a second Microsoft product, PowerPoint, and 'pointless' strips POINT from it.
explanation.definitionFit: China is an example of a dominant nation with global influence, which is what a world power is.

clue.text: Universal ID traps down-and-outs

indicators.note: traps means holds inside, so the universal letter is enclosed

parts.note: papers are identity documents, ID
U is the film classification for universal, suitable for all

explanation.surface: A universal identity card scheme catches out homeless people.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the British film certificate meaning suitable for everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: Paupers are very poor people with no means, which is what down-and-outs are.

clue.text: Design plug-in memory device on a phone, originally

indicators.note: in means the advert letters go inside the memory letters

parts.note: ROM is read-only memory
a plug is an advertisement, an ad

indicators.note: originally means only the first letter of the word is used

parts.note: first letter taken

explanation.surface: Technical talk about adding a plug-in memory module to a phone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plug-in' reads as one technical word but splits: a plug is an advert, and 'in' places it inside ROM.
explanation.definitionFit: A road map is a plan setting out the steps to a goal, so it is a design for what will happen.

clue.text: Possessing heroin — after comedian…

indicators.note: after means the heroin letter comes later, following the comedian

parts.note: a wit is a clever, funny person
H is drug slang for heroin

explanation.surface: A comedian is caught carrying heroin, with the story continuing in the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs the surface on into the next clue; it plays no part in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: With as a preposition can mean having, as in a man with a beard, a sense of owning something.

clue.text: …mostly performs at clubs potentially developing habit?

indicators.note: mostly means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: to play is to perform
clubs is one example of a suit in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: Continuing from the previous clue, the comedian mostly plays clubs and may be forming a drug habit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Habit' looks like the drug addiction of the previous clue but means clothing; 'developing' points to a young child, who wears this garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A playsuit is a one-piece outfit for a small child, and habit is an old word for dress or costume.

clue.text: Funny ending to Freddie Starr's book

indicators.note: funny means odd or peculiar, so the letters are rearranged
ending to means take the final letter of the name that follows

parts.note: last letter taken
taken as written

explanation.surface: A comedian's memoir has a funny last chapter; Freddie Starr was a British comedian.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after Starr is 'is', a link, not a possessive; 'book' is a verb, as when police book someone.
explanation.definitionFit: When police book someone they formally charge them, taking them into custody, which is to arrest them.

clue.text: Grubby, like a pomegranate …

definitions.meaning: second meaning: full of seeds, as a pomegranate is

explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links into the next clue, adding to the fruit theme with mandarin orange; it does no work here.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both sleazy or dirty, and literally containing many seeds, as the fruit does.

clue.text: Bishop discovered card game on vacation — perhaps pontoon

parts.note: B is the chess notation for bishop

indicators.note: discovered means uncovered, so the word loses its outer letters

parts.note: middle letters taken

indicators.note: on vacation means emptied, so only the outside letters of the word remain

parts.note: first and last letters taken

explanation.surface: A bishop on holiday is caught playing the card game pontoon.
explanation.walkthrough: Pontoon looks like the card game, given the cards around it, but here means a flat-bottomed boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A pontoon is a flat-bottomed boat or float, and a barge is a similar flat-bottomed vessel.

clue.text: Dancer maybe receiving marks — wanting third judge's conclusion to be prompt

indicators.note: receiving means taking in, so the marks letter goes inside
wanting means lacking, so the letter is removed
third picks which of the three matching letters in the reindeer's name goes

parts.note: Dancer is one of Santa's reindeer

indicators.note: conclusion means the end, so only the final letter of judge is used

parts.note: last letter taken
M is the abbreviation for marks, the old German currency

explanation.surface: A dancer on a talent show waits for the marks, with the third judge yet to give a verdict.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dancer' looks like a performer but is Santa's reindeer. REINDEER has three Es; the third goes, then M is put inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A reminder is something that jogs the memory, just as a prompt nudges someone to recall a line.

clue.text: … and not mandarin orange segment

indicators.note: a segment is a piece, here a run of letters taken from inside the words

parts.note: the letters are found across these words

explanation.surface: Following the pomegranate, a citrus segment is turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Segment' is a fruit piece in the surface but marks the hidden run spanning the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Nor is a conjunction introducing a further negative, carrying the sense of also not.

clue.text: So angry about agent coming back with terms for another Harry Potter

indicators.note: about means around, so these letters are turned around into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: coming back means the agent word is read in reverse

parts.note: a rep, short for representative, is a sales agent

indicators.note: terms are ends or limits, so each of the two words gives its final letter

parts.note: last letter taken
last letter taken

explanation.surface: Someone is cross that an agent is returning with a deal for another Harry Potter book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harry Potter' wants to be the boy wizard, but Potter alone is the definition: a maker of pottery.
explanation.definitionFit: Grayson Perry is a Turner Prize-winning English artist famous for his ceramic vases, a potter by trade.
